Triage (maintainer-authorized one-off pass, 2026-08-09, registered on #6015): **promoted `finding` → `pm:queue`** (`domain:drivers` kept). Direction note per precedent, not a new ruling: #3724 already decided this exact shape (a driver face that boots but silently fails to deliver a declared capability) with disposition **B — explicit refusal**; the deliverable here is the same: `auto_number`-bearing objects on the Turso remote transport fail loudly at create instead of silently writing nothing. Implementing autonumber on remote (A) stays behind the appetite door — no demand measured. #6932's absence-assertion already guards against a silent half-implementation.

Claim: PM loop, drivers lane — dispatched under the maintainer's standing authorization of 2026-08-08 ~17:15Z and their 2026-08-09 ~14:0xZ reaffirmation (「继续派发,并优先 v17 的任务」).

Session: `session_01Hg9Pkg5nDedCRihRsdeCdX`
Branch: `claude/issue-6944-turso-remote-autonumber-refusal`
Worktree: `objectstack-issue-6944` (cloud session — own container, Opus)

**A correction to this seat's own record first.** I had this card listed as *blocked pending an A-or-B ruling*, and said so in the seat status (comment `5230719256`). That was wrong: triage **already ruled** at 06:46Z in comment `5230216863` — disposition **B**, explicit refusal, with A ("implement autonumber on remote") explicitly left behind the appetite door for want of measured demand. I had read this issue's body, which poses A/B, and not its comment. It is the second time today that not re-reading a thread cost something — on #6943 it made me contradict a scope fence; here it idled a dispatchable card for seven hours.

**On v17 priority.** Measured again at 14:0xZ across 25 open issues, intersected by hand (the label filter is OR, not AND): `target:v17` ∩ `domain:drivers` is **zero**. The v17 cards on the board today are `domain:cli` (#7033, #7023, #6599), `domain:devx` (#7005), `domain:metadata` (#6190), objectui (#6955, #5175, #5149) and cloud (#6954, #5852) — none of them this seat's to take. So the priority has no object here and this card goes next on queue order.

**Serial constraint.** `main` @ `fa6b4362a`; nothing open touches `driver-turso`. ⚠️ Note #7011 was fixed by another party while this seat was unattended (`d2544215e`, PR #7059) — re-check before claiming anything else.

### Premise re-verified on `fa6b4362a` (anchors by content, not line)

- `RemoteTransport` — `packages/drivers/driver-turso/src/remote-transport.ts:763`; its `create` at `:1090`, which builds its own INSERT.
- Routing — `turso-driver.ts:226` (`transportMode === 'remote'`), `:388` (`isRemote()`).
- The absence is already pinned by #6932 in `turso-autonumber-resync.test.ts:13` and `:73`.

### The deliverable, quoting the ruling

> `auto_number`-bearing objects on the Turso remote transport fail loudly at create instead of silently writing nothing.

⛔ Not the dev's choice to re-litigate. If implementation turns up evidence that B is wrong or infeasible, **stop and report** — do not switch to A.

### ⚠️ The trap specific to this card

#6932's absence assertion currently pins *"`RemoteTransport` has no autonumber surface at all"*. After this change the shape becomes **explicitly refused**, not absent — so that assertion must be **rewritten to pin the refusal, not deleted**. Deleting it removes the very guard that stops a future silent half-implementation; leaving it unchanged makes it assert something no longer true. This is the same class as #6792's false docstring and #6943's burn comment: the stale statement is the last place a wrong fact survives.

Also to settle by measurement, not assumption: whether `RemoteTransport.create` can even see the object schema it would need in order to know a field is `auto_number`. If it cannot, the refusal has to be raised where that knowledge exists — say so rather than reaching for it.

### Refusal shape

Unlike #6943's layer, this refusal is one **we author**, so ADR-0112 applies in full: assert `code` **and** `status`, never a bare `toThrow` (#6144). Follow the existing driver precedent rather than inventing an envelope — `UnsupportedDriverError` is the shape #3724/route-B used for "this driver cannot honour what you asked for".

Scope: `driver-turso` only. local/replica inherit `SqlDriver` and are **unaffected** — pin that they still work, so the refusal cannot leak onto the wrong face (#6203). `driver-memory`/`driver-mongodb` are inside the #5499 freeze and declare no `supports.autonumber`; genuinely unrelated.

## os-dev report

**Card:** #6944 · **PR:** #7089 (left **draft** — not marked ready, no auto-merge) · **Branch:** `claude/issue-6944-turso-remote-autonumber-refusal` · **Base:** `main` @ `2f3e79351` (the clone's tip; `fa6b4362a` had already been passed by the time this seat cloned — `origin/main` has since moved to `4e6ca32`, and none of the three intervening commits touch `packages/drivers/**`, so no rebase was needed).

---

### 1. `premise_still_valid` — **yes**, re-measured, not inherited

Every anchor re-derived by content on `2f3e79351`, and the defect reproduced end-to-end against a real SQLite wearing the `@libsql/client` interface (`libsql-sqlite-stub.testkit.ts`), not asserted from reading:

```
P1 transportMode on libsql://       -> 'remote'
P5 REMOTE create                    -> RESOLVED case_number=null
P7 REMOTE bulkCreate (2 rows)       -> RESOLVED [null, null]
P8 REMOTE upsert                    -> RESOLVED case_number=null
P6 physical column type             -> case_number TEXT
P10 LOCAL create                    -> RESOLVED case_number="CASE-00001"
```

`RemoteTransport` at `remote-transport.ts:763`, its `create` at `:1090` building its own `INSERT`; routing at `turso-driver.ts:226` / `:388`. Confirmed.

One measurement worth adding to the premise, because it explains why nothing upstream catches this: **`supports.autonumber` is `true` on the remote face** (inherited through `...super.supports`), so `engine.ts` defers generation to the driver entirely and never runs its own fallback. `engine.ts`'s own driver table already records `driver-turso` as "inherited (`...super.supports`) · fallback path? **no**". The engine is doing exactly what it was told; the declaration is what is false.

### 2. Which layer the refusal lands on, and why — **settled by measurement**

**`RemoteTransport` cannot see the object schema.** `create(object, data)` — arity **2**, measured — takes no schema, and the class caches none: `syncSchema` / `syncSchemasBatch` read a schema, emit DDL and keep nothing. It cannot tell an `auto_number` column from any other `TEXT` one.

**`TursoDriver` can, in remote mode.** `initObjects`/`syncSchema` call `registerRemoteFieldMetadata` → `SqlDriver.registerExternalObject`, which classifies every field and populates `autoNumberFields` keyed by **object name** (`key = schema.name`). Measured live on a remote-mode driver:

```
autoNumberFields['crm_case'] ->
  [{ name:'case_number', format:'CASE-{00000}', tokens:[…], tenantField:'organization_id' }]
```

So the refusal is raised **on the driver**, in the remote branch of `create` / `bulkCreate` / `upsert`, and nothing was reached for from a layer that does not hold the knowledge. Both halves are pinned as assertions in the new suite, so the decision stays reviewable if either fact moves.

The lookup deliberately has **no table-name fallback** (unlike `fillAutoNumberFields`): in remote mode the only writer of that registry is `registerRemoteFieldMetadata`, whose own docs record that it keys strictly by `object`, and the Knex path that produces the other key is unreachable there. A second lookup rule would be a second answer.

### 3. The envelope — **`UnsupportedDriverError` is the wrong shape here; I read it before deciding**

The brief pointed at `UnsupportedDriverError` as "#3724 / route-B's shape". Measured: today that class lives in **`packages/cli/src/utils/storage-driver.ts`**, is exported by the CLI only, and answers a different question — *"this driver **selection** cannot become a driver instance"* (`--database-driver sqlite3`; `turso` with no URL). Its own docblock says so, and its second consumer is a CLI allowlist pin test that reads `driverType` off it. `@objectstack/driver-turso` does not depend on `@objectstack/cli` and must not: that would invert the dependency to raise a runtime write error.

The **existing driver precedent** for "this backend cannot honour what you asked for" is the one this very package already uses, twice: `NOT_IMPLEMENTED` / **501**, per ADR-0112 and the #5907 two-class taxonomy — class 1 (`INVALID_QUERY`/400) is a caller mistake, class 2 (`NOT_IMPLEMENTED`/501) is a capability gap in the backend for something the spec declares and other backends deliver (`uncompilableAggregateFunctionError`, `refuseDateBucketedGroupBy`). `autonumber` is a declared field type that **this very driver's other two faces generate**, so the object definition is correct and the gap is the backend's. That is class 2, verbatim.

Refused **before the statement is built**, so a refused write costs no round trip — asserted (zero `execute` calls, row count unchanged), matching the rule every other refusal on this path follows.

### 4. #6932's assertion — **rewritten to pin the refusal. And there were two, not one.**

The brief named `turso-autonumber-resync.test.ts` (#6932). While re-deriving I found **a second, identical absence-assertion**: `turso-autonumber-batch-resync.test.ts` (#6943), whose docblock even says *"(That gap is #6944's, not this card's.)"* Same trap, same treatment — leaving it would have been the exact failure the brief warned about, one file over.

Both were pinning *"`RemoteTransport` has no autonumber surface at all"* — literally still true after this change (I added nothing to the transport), but standing next to a claim that is no longer whole: *"so it neither has this defect nor receives this fix … `auto_number` is only a column-type mapping"*. Deleting either removes the only guard against a future half-implementation landing quietly **inside the transport**; leaving either unchanged keeps a green assertion beside a stale fact.

So each keeps its surface probe **verbatim** and gains the other half:

- `turso-autonumber-resync.test.ts` → `REMOTE: … still has no autonumber machinery to re-seed` (unchanged probe) **+** `REMOTE: [#6944] and having none, it refuses the create rather than writing nothing` — `code` **and** `status`.
- `turso-autonumber-batch-resync.test.ts` → same, with the refusal asserted on **`bulkCreate`** specifically, because Turso overrides it and `RemoteTransport.bulkCreate` loops its **own** `create` — "`create` refuses" is not on its own an answer about that path.

Both docblocks carry a `⚠️ [#6944] rewritten, not deleted` section stating the two wrong options and why. And both now go **red** under the revert (§9), which is the operational proof they pin the fact rather than describe it.

### 5. local / replica — **unaffected, and pinned**

Nothing in `SqlDriver` was touched, and the refusal sits strictly inside `if (this.isRemote)` branches. Pinned positively rather than argued:

- `LOCAL create` → `CASE-00001`
- `LOCAL bulkCreate` → `['CASE-00001','CASE-00002']`, `LOCAL upsert` → `CASE-00003`
- `REPLICA create` (`:memory:` + `syncUrl`, mode asserted `'replica'`) → `CASE-00001`
- the two pre-existing local re-seed suites (#5495, #6943, incl. the #7011 merge-upsert pin) still green, untouched

### 6. Three faces — declared

`local` / `replica` / `remote` are each exercised in the new suite, by construction and with `transportMode` asserted on each. The refusal is proved present on exactly one face and absent from the other two (#6203: a fix that lands on one face is one query with two answers).

### 7. #5499 frozen faces — declared

`driver-memory` and `driver-mongodb` were **not touched and are genuinely unrelated**: neither declares `supports.autonumber`, so both take the **engine's own** in-memory fallback (`engine.ts` `generateAutoNumbers`), a different mechanism from the SQL family's persistent sequence. Nothing in this change reaches them. `driver-sql` and `driver-sqlite-wasm` also untouched — the change is `packages/drivers/driver-turso` only, plus one changeset.

### 8. Gates and tests — per job

**CI on `584eacd` (PR #7089): 23 `success`, 2 `skipped`, 0 `failure`, 0 `in_progress`.**

- `success` (23): ESLint · TypeScript Type Check · Build Core · Test Core (+ 1/3, 2/3, 3/3) · Dogfood Regression Gate (+ 1/3, 2/3, 3/3) · Dogfood Verify CLI · Temporal Conformance (live PG + MySQL) · **Check Changeset** · Check PR Size · Check Documentation Links · Flag docs affected by code changes · Console Pin Freshness · ADR maintainer approval · No other open PR may claim the same issue · Auto Label · filter · Vercel Preview Comments
- `skipped` (2), both named and structural — neither can be `success` on this diff:
  - **Build Docs** — `ci.yml`'s `docs` paths-filter is `apps/docs/**`, `content/**`, `pnpm-lock.yaml`, `.github/workflows/ci.yml`. This diff touches none.
  - **Console Pin Gate** — the `console` filter is `.objectui-sha`, `scripts/build-console.sh`, `scripts/check-console-sha.mjs`, `.github/workflows/ci.yml`. This diff touches none.

**Changeset:** product code changed, so a **real changeset** was written (`.changeset/turso-remote-autonumber-refusal.md`, `@objectstack/driver-turso: minor` — a deliberate behaviour change, not a silent-repair patch; `major` is blocked by `check:changeset-no-major`). The `skip-changeset` label was **not** used and is not applicable. `Check Changeset` is `success`, not `skipped`.

**Locally, enumerated live from `.github/workflows/lint.yml` (not from memory) — 46 `check:*` gates + 23 build/typecheck steps, all pass:**

- all 46 lint-job gates pass, including `check:tenant-chokepoint` (#6908), `check:query-options-erasure` (the **bidirectional** ratchet — count unmoved in both directions), `check:error-code-casing`, `check:driver-conformance`, `check:driver-memory-census`, `check:published-files`, `check:type-check-coverage`, `check:changeset-gate-self-tests`
- `turbo run build --filter='./packages/*' --filter='./examples/*^...'` · `turbo run typecheck --filter='./packages/*' --filter='./packages/*/*' --filter='./apps/*'` · `turbo run build --filter='./packages/*' --filter='./packages/*/*'` · `check:type-check-debt` · **`examples` typecheck** · **`downstream-contract` typecheck** · all nine `@objectstack/spec` gates · `check:i18n`, `check:i18n-coverage`, `check:app-nav-i18n`
- **Tests:** `driver-turso` **33 files / 931 tests, all green** (17 new in `turso-remote-autonumber-refusal.test.ts`, 2 added to the rewritten pins). Reported below rather than tidied: the three i18n gates failed on the **first** local pass with `PREREQUISITE NOT MET — the workspace CLI is not built` (they run after the build step in CI); they pass after the build. That is an ordering artefact of running the list out of CI order, not a result about the change — recorded because "I re-ran it and it was fine" is exactly the sentence that hides a real red.

### 9. Reverse verification — predictions written **before** the runs

**Round 0 (baseline probe, 10 predictions).** All 10 matched, including the two that decided the design: `autoNumberFields` **is** populated in remote mode (P3), and `RemoteTransport.create` has arity 2 with no schema (P4).

**Round 2 (upsert shapes, 5 predictions).** All 5 matched: a remote upsert with no `id` **always inserts** (two calls → two rows, different ids, so the transport's fresh nanoid can never match its sole default merge key); an `id`-bearing upsert onto an existing row **merges and keeps** `CASE-00042`; `update` never needs a number; the no-autonumber control is untouched; local upsert keeps `CASE-00001`.

**Round 3 (the revert).** Predicted: with `refuseUngeneratableRemoteAutonumber`'s body emptied, every REMOTE refusal case fails through the harness's *"it resolved"* branch — **not** on a `code`/`status` comparison, because the un-fixed code never threw — while the pass-through block, the residue pin and all three faces' controls stay green.

Measured: **`8 failed | 923 passed`**, and the prediction held — the 6 cases in the new suite plus the **2 rewritten pins**, all through "it resolved" / "expected a refusal"; the 11 cases outside the refusal block stayed green.

**Not predicted, kept rather than tidied:** the reverted suite does not merely go red, it **reprints the defect** — every failure message carries the resolved row with `"case_number":null` inside it (and `""` for the empty-string case). That is a property worth knowing: the next person to break this reads the bug off the failure line without opening a file.

### 10. Out-of-scope findings — recorded, **not** fixed

1. **`supports.autonumber` is a false capability on the remote face.** It is inherited `true` while that face generates nothing — the *same* argument `turso-driver.ts` already makes ten lines away for `queryDateGranularity: {}` in remote mode, which it calls "a FALSE capability" in those words. **I deliberately did not flip it**, and the reason is load-bearing: `supports.autonumber === false` routes the engine to its **own** in-memory autonumber fallback, which would then generate numbers on the remote face — i.e. it delivers option **A** by another road, the one triage explicitly left behind the appetite door. Flipping that bit is an appetite decision, not a cleanup, so it is filed here rather than taken.
2. **Upsert residue (also pinned in-suite).** An upsert that carries an `id` or explicit `conflictKeys` but matches nothing still **inserts**, and on that leg the slot is still written NULL. Classifying it needs the round trip the refusal exists to avoid. Pinned as a `[known residue, not fixed]` assertion so it cannot quietly change in either direction.
3. `turso-driver.ts`'s licence header reads `Copyright (c) 2025` while every other file in the package reads `2026`. Pre-existing, one line, untouched.

### 11. Open questions for the PM / maintainer

1. **Should the remote face declare `supports.autonumber: false`?** As above, that is not a documentation fix — it hands generation to the engine's fallback and is A in disguise. If the appetite door stays shut, the declaration stays knowingly false and the refusal is what makes it honest at the call site. Worth an explicit ruling either way, because "declared ≠ enforced" is ADR-0049's whole subject.
2. **Is the upsert residue (§10.2) acceptable as shipped**, or does it want its own card alongside the deferred A?
3. `minor` vs `patch` on the changeset: I chose `minor` because a caller on remote + `auto_number` now gets a 501 where it previously got a row. Say the word if the repo's convention for a refusal-that-replaces-wrong-behaviour is `patch` (#6409's `count_distinct` used `patch`).

PR left **draft** for the step-7 gate.

## PM acceptance — ACCEPTED, PR #7089

Your three questions first, then the gate.

### 1. `supports.autonumber: false` — **no. Do not flip it.**

Ruled, and I verified your reasoning independently before agreeing rather than taking it. `engine.ts:2465`:

```js
if (driverOwnsAutonumber) return []; // driver generates persistently in create()
```

So `supports.autonumber === false` on the remote face does not document a gap — it **routes generation to the engine's own in-memory fallback**, which would then issue numbers on a transport that has no `_objectstack_sequences` table at all. That is disposition **A** by the back door, on the worst possible path, and it is precisely what triage parked behind the appetite door. You were right to name the flip as an appetite decision rather than a cleanup, and right not to take it.

So the declaration stays knowingly false at the capability level, and the refusal is what makes it honest at the call site. When the appetite door opens for A, that bit flips *with* the implementation, not before it. I am leaving this ruling here rather than in a new card because it must stay attached to the card that explains it.

### 2. `minor` vs `patch` — **`minor` stands.**

Your instinct is right and the counter-precedent you raised does not transfer. #6409's `count_distinct` was `patch` because it corrected a **computation** to match the declared contract: callers getting wrong numbers started getting right ones, and nothing that succeeded began to fail. Every other patch this lane shipped today (#6792, #5495, #6943, #6754) has that same shape — promised behaviour restored, no new failure mode.

This one deliberately introduces one: a caller on remote with an `auto_number` field previously got a row and now gets a 501. Surfacing a pre-existing breakage is still a behaviour change at the call site, and `minor` is what signals it.

### 3. Upsert residue — **acceptable as shipped**, and filed as **#7099** so it survives this card's closure.

The trade is real and correctly reasoned: classifying that leg needs the round trip the refusal exists to avoid, and the refusal's zero-round-trip property is worth keeping. Your in-suite `[known residue, not fixed]` pin is the right treatment — it cannot drift silently in either direction. #7099 records it for triage; no action wanted from you.

### Where you overrode me, with evidence, and were right

**The envelope.** I pointed you at `UnsupportedDriverError` as "#3724 / route-B's shape". I checked after reading your rebuttal: it lives in `packages/cli/src/utils/storage-driver.ts`, is CLI-only, and answers *"this driver **selection** cannot become an instance"* — a different question. `driver-turso`'s `package.json` has **no** dependency on `@objectstack/cli`, so following my instruction would have inverted the dependency to raise a runtime write error. `NOT_IMPLEMENTED` / 501 per ADR-0112 and the #5907 two-class taxonomy is the in-family precedent, documented in this driver family's own source at `sql-driver.ts:699` and already used by `refuseAggregateFunction` and the date-bucket refusals. Your choice is correct and mine was written from memory without checking. Third time today a dev has falsified one of my dispatch facts with measurement; each time the instruction was worth less than the check.

**The second absence assertion.** I named `turso-autonumber-resync.test.ts` (#6932). You found `turso-autonumber-batch-resync.test.ts` (#6943) carrying the identical claim — its docblock even says *"(That gap is #6944's, not this card's.)"* — and treated it the same way. That is the trap I warned about, one file over from where I pointed.

### Verified independently

| Criterion | Result |
|---|---|
| `premise_still_valid` | ✅ reproduced end-to-end against a real SQLite wearing the `@libsql/client` interface — `create`/`bulkCreate`/`upsert` all resolved with `case_number=null`, local returned `CASE-00001` |
| refusal raised where the knowledge lives | ✅ **measured, not assumed**: `RemoteTransport.create` has arity 2 and caches no schema; `TursoDriver` holds `autoNumberFields` via `registerRemoteFieldMetadata`. Both halves pinned as assertions so the decision stays reviewable |
| both assertions rewritten, not deleted | ✅ each keeps its surface probe **verbatim** and gains the refusal half, with a `⚠️ [#6944] rewritten, not deleted` note stating the two wrong options |
| `code` **and** `status` | ✅ `NOT_IMPLEMENTED` / 501, never a bare `toThrow` |
| local/replica unaffected | ✅ pinned positively on all three faces with `transportMode` asserted on each, not argued from the base class |
| #5499 freeze | ✅ untouched and genuinely unrelated |
| CI | ✅ 23 success, 2 skipped, 0 failure, 0 in_progress — and each skip justified by naming the actual paths-filter globs it misses |

**The revert is what makes this convincing.** 8 failed / 923 passed, matching the prediction that failures land in the *"it resolved"* branch rather than on a `code` comparison — because un-fixed code never threw. And the unpredicted property you kept rather than tidied: the reverted suite **reprints the defect**, carrying `"case_number":null` inside each failure message. The next person to break this reads the bug off the failure line.

Also noted: recording that the three i18n gates went red on the first local pass for a build-ordering reason, instead of quietly re-running — *"I re-ran it and it was fine"* is exactly the sentence that hides a real red.

Marking ready and enabling auto-merge.
